overview.heading: What is B.Com?
paragraphs: B.Com, or Bachelor of Commerce, is a three-year undergraduate degree in commerce that usually follows Class 12. It covers the basics of accounting, economics, business law, taxation, finance, and related business subjects, so students learn how money, records, markets, and organisations work in everyday business life.

The course suits students who are comfortable with numbers, careful reading, and regular practice. Learning is usually a mix of theory, problem-solving, case studies, and practical business concepts. It can lead to work in accounting, banking, taxation, audit, finance, business operations, or further professional study after graduation.

B.Com is a broad foundation, not a single job track. A graduate’s earnings depend on the job role, city, employer, internships, and extra qualifications. Students who plan to add courses such as CA, CS, CFA, or similar credentials often have more options and stronger pay growth than those relying on the degree alone.

snapshot.data_note: B.Com pay in India changes with the job, city, employer, internships, and extra qualifications. Entry roles are often around INR 200000 to INR 400000 a year, while stronger early-career outcomes can reach roughly INR 800000 or more in specialised finance and commerce roles.

salary.note: A common early-career range for B.Com graduates in India is about INR 200000 to INR 800000 a year, with the middle of the market often around INR 400000. Professional credentials and role choice can move pay well above this band.

points: A B.Com degree alone does not guarantee a high-paying job; many better-paid roles need extra qualifications or postgraduate study.

curriculum.assessment_methods: End-semester written exams, internal tests, class presentations, case studies, practical assignments, project work, and in some colleges a dissertation or research project in the final year.
curriculum.learning_activities: Lectures, tutorials, problem-solving exercises, accounting practice, case studies, spreadsheet-based tasks, group discussions, seminars, and project or internship-based learning in the final year.

parent_corner.intro: B.Com is a practical undergraduate option for students who are comfortable with numbers, business ideas, and regular reading and writing. It can lead toward accounting, banking, taxation, audit, finance, and operations work, but it is not a licence for regulated careers such as CA, CMA, or CS. Families should treat B.Com as a base degree: the college matters, but so do the student’s habits, communication skills, and later choices. In school years, steady progress in mathematics, accounts, English, and computer use helps a lot. By Class 11-12, the key decisions are the stream, the college list, and whether the student wants a general B.Com or a more specialised honours track.
